title: Strix: WYSIWYG math for engineers
description: Strix is an open-source document editor for math and engineering problems, written in Rust. Equations typed in the page calculate live, with units, solving, checks, exercises and CAD drawings driven by the results. Windows, macOS, Linux, BSD and the web.
socialAlt: Strix: type the equation, it calculates
heroLead: Strix is a document editor for math and engineering problems. The equations you write in the page are live: they carry units, solve for the unknown, check limits and update the moment an input changes.
heroNote: Free and open source (MIT or Apache-2.0) · Windows · macOS · Linux · FreeBSD · web · no account, no telemetry
shotCalcAlt: Strix with a beam calculation: span and load with units, the bending moment computed from q·L²/8, the stress and a stress check with a tick
stat1Text: defines, shows, solves or checks: Strix works out which
stat2Text: SI and engineering units, checked on every step
stat3Text: results, tables, exercises and drawings recalculate after each edit
stat4Text: interface languages, on five platforms from one Rust code base
howTitle: Write the problem as on paper. The page does the arithmetic.
a1Text: No code cells, no formula bar, no separate sheet. Strix reads the calculated equations in reading order and keeps every result current, waiting until the caret leaves an equation so nothing changes under your typing.
a2Text: L = 4.5 m defines, M = q·L²/8 = shows the value, F = m·a solves for the one unknown, σ ≤ f_yd checks and shows ✓ or ✗.
a3Text: Quantities, not numbers: SI and engineering units with prefixes, dimensionless units kept, results in the unit you last wrote. 2 m + 3 s is an error, never a silent wrong answer.
a4Text: Results, tables, exercises and drawings stay live in the .xmath file, a standard package other programs open with the last computed values. Static copies go to PDF, PNG, LaTeX, HTML and Markdown. Word, ODT and RTF files open and save back as long as they hold no calculations, exercises or drawings; with any, Strix saves .xmath, so nothing live is lost.
mathIntro: An equation typed with the equation editor is typeset like any other, and it is the calculation. Errors never stop the sheet: a failing statement shows ⚠ and its message, and the rest still calculates.
math1: Solving: the unknown is isolated symbolically when it appears once (powers, roots, exp, ln, trigonometry), found numerically otherwise.
math2: Units are typeset upright and coloured, converted to the working unit, with a hint for the wrong case (“did you mean kN?”).
math3: Solution steps: the formula solved for the unknown, the values substituted, the result, aligned at =.
math4: Calculated tables: headers name columns with units and formulas, Σ = totals them, every column becomes a vector.
math5: Sums, ranges and vectors: ∑, ∏, i = 1..5, [1; 2; 3] kN, with a number format by digits, decimals or significant figures.
mathFigureLabel: Solving, units and a calculated table in a Strix document
tableCaption: A calculated table: columns with units and formulas, a total, every column a vector afterwards.
featTitle: A calculation notebook that is also a real document
featIntro: What is in Strix today. Planned work is marked as planned.
f1Text: Every calculated equation and table is re-evaluated after each edit, on F9 and when the file opens. Change one input and every result, check and drawing that depends on it follows.
f2Title: Write the relation, get the unknown
f2Text: F = m·a with F and m known gives a. Comparisons ≤ ≥ < > ≠ verify limits with ✓ or ✗.
f3Text: SI and engineering units with prefixes, dimensionless units kept, working units, case hints.
f4Text: Statement, data, nested questions, a solution under each question, variants and one results summary.
f5Text: Coordinates are expressions of parameters; dimensions show their values; change <var>L</var> and the drawing follows.
f6Text: Rule a page or a block in squares, with heavier lines every N squares, sharp at any zoom and in PDF.
f7Text: Ribbon interface, styles, lists, tables, footnotes, citations, comments, track changes, spelling, printing.
f8Text: Saves .xmath, and DOCX, ODT, RTF back when a document has no Strix objects; opens DOCX, DOC, ODT, RTF, HTML, Markdown, LaTeX; exports PDF, PNG, LaTeX, HTML, Markdown.
f9Title: Native on every desktop, and in the browser
f9Text: Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD as native apps, and the same app compiled to WebAssembly. The interface follows the system’s language (27 languages) and its light or dark theme.
plannedText: Variables pane, unit picker, °C/°F, user functions f(x) = …, matrices, systems of equations, plots; CAD modify tools, hatches, angular dimensions and constraints.
exTitle: Problems with a structure you can’t break
exIntro: Math › Exercise inserts a worked problem held together by locked parts: you write freely inside them, and the skeleton stays.
ex1: Statement, data and questions, lettered and nested to three levels (a), a.1), a.1.1)), with notes between them.
ex2: The solution repeats each question as a read-only line, with its working under it, and follows the questions when they change.
ex3: A sandbox: what an exercise defines stays inside it, so two exercises can both use L.
ex4: Data and variants A, B, C… in the Exercise Properties pane: picking a variant recalculates everything.
ex5: One results summary at the end of the document lists every marked result with its value.
shotExerciseAlt: A Strix exercise: title, statement, data, lettered questions and the solution worked under each question
cadIntro: A CAD drawing sits in the text like a picture, but its coordinates can be expressions of the parameters defined above it. Change L = 4.5m and the beam redraws; its dimension reads the new value.
cad1: Labels from parameters: {{L}} shows 4.5 m, {{L:both}} shows L = 4.5 m, <> the measured size.
cad2: An editor on the drawing’s sheet: lines, circles, arcs, polylines, rectangles, texts and dimensions, with a command line for coordinates.
cad3: Exact snaps on the true curves (endpoint, midpoint, centre, intersection, perpendicular, tangent…) from a geometry kernel tested to 1e-9.
cad4: Grips reshape objects and keep the expressions: L becomes L + 0.5.
cad5: Properties and layers: colour, lineweight, linetype, and the geometry as numbers or expressions. Saved with an SVG picture, so other programs still show it.
cadFigureLabel: A parametric beam drawing whose span dimension shows L = 4.5 m
cadCaption: The beam’s end point is the expression ["L", 0]: change L and the drawing and its dimension follow.
agTitle: Built to be driven by people and by agents
agIntro: Everything Strix does is a command with an id and parameters. The ribbon, keyboard shortcuts, command search, the command line, a local control channel and the MCP server all run the same commands, and programmatic calls never open dialogs.
agNote: The control channel and the MCP server listen on 127.0.0.1 only and need a per-window key; an agent can be confined to chosen folders.
dlIntro: Installers and portable builds for every platform. Strix is in alpha: keep a copy of important documents, and tell us what breaks.
dlWindowsNote: Windows 10 and 11. The builds are not code-signed yet: SmartScreen may warn on first run. The portable exe needs no installation and keeps its settings in a StrixData folder beside it.
dlMacNote: One universal build for Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
dlLinuxNote: x86_64 and aarch64; riscv64 as deb, rpm and tar.gz.
dlBsdNote: The app and the command line, with licences and icons.
dlWebNote: The same app compiled to WebAssembly: nothing to install. The ZIP is a static site you can host yourself.
t1Text: Strix sends nothing on its own: no usage data, no crash reports, no update check. Documents and preferences stay on your computer.
t2Text: Production code has no unwrap, expect or unsafe; every command is tested with hostile parameters, and recovery copies protect open documents.
t3Text: A .xmath file is a standard OOXML package. Exports to PDF, LaTeX, HTML and Markdown keep your work readable anywhere.
t4Text: MIT or Apache-2.0, developed in the open, with every bundled font, dictionary and translation attributed.
startTitle: Build it and open the sample
startIntro: You need a Rust toolchain (1.95 or later); the web build also needs Trunk and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target.
startWeb: Or run it in the browser
startThen: Then open the Math tab, choose New Calculation, type L = 4.5 m and keep going. Design notes:
